Hong Kong Fisheries Industry Hit by Major Cyber Attack; Operations Disrupted

A widespread cyber attack has struck several firms within Hong Kong’s fisheries industry, causing severe operational disruptions and raising concerns about the sector’s resilience to digital threats. The attack, which began late Monday night, appears to involve ransomware targeting the information technology systems of both onshore processing facilities and offshore fleet operators.

According to the Hong Kong Fisheries Association, at least six medium and large fisheries companies, including South Harbour Seafood Ltd and Ocean Star Fisheries, have reported significant IT outages. “Our members’ ability to coordinate catch schedules, process orders, and manage inventory has been substantially hindered,” said Chairperson Lau Kin-wai. “We are working closely with authorities, but the situation is ongoing and urgent.”

Affected companies have reported that their computer networks were rendered inaccessible, with attackers demanding payment in cryptocurrency to restore access. As a result, fisheries workers have been unable to access electronic records essential for sorting and processing catches, leading to delays at fish landing sites in Aberdeen and Castle Peak. “We are currently sorting fish by hand and using paper logs. It’s slow and mistakes are happening,” said Lee Wai-man, a site supervisor at the Aberdeen Fish Wharf.

Industry analysts estimate that the disruption could affect up to 40 percent of daily seafood output if the attack continues through the week. “Fisheries are increasingly reliant on digital tracking for vessel coordination and temperature-controlled storage. Losing these systems even for a few days can have a major impact,” said Dr. Fiona Chan, a supply chain expert at Hong Kong Maritime University.

Workers in the sector have voiced concerns about job security and pay as overtime is required to manage the backlog. “We’re worried that if this goes on, catches will spoil and we won’t get paid,” said Chan Ho-lam, a fish processing worker.

Authorities from the Hong Kong Fisheries Protection Department have confirmed that an investigation is underway but declined to provide further details due to the sensitive nature of the incident. As of Tuesday evening, no timeline had been given for restoring normal operations, and the attack remains unresolved. The Fisheries Association has urged all firms in the industry to review their cybersecurity practices as the threat continues.
